da-false-claim.evidence: The proof claims 'The trace and volume map are linear on the Hecke algebra', allowing it to write $\mathrm{Vol}(\overline{\gamma}) = \mathrm{Vol}(\overline{1}) + \sum \phi_i \mathrm{Vol}(\overline{\sigma_i})$. This is a mathematically false claim. Hyperbolic volume is a highly non-linear geometric invariant of the link complement; it does not extend linearly across linear combinations in the Hecke algebra.

da-non-sequitur.evidence: proof:21-22 'The trace and volume map are linear on the Hecke algebra' is false: H_3 is spanned by positive permutation braids whose closures are unlinks/unknot/Hopf link (Vol 0), so linearity would force Vol(closure σ₁σ₂⁻¹σ₁σ₂⁻¹ = 4_1) = 0, but Vol(4_1) = 2.0299

da-non-sequitur.evidence: Full review 2026-11-21. Cases 1-2 are correct: the closures of 1 and s_i^{+-1} are an n-component and an (n-1)-component unlink, non-hyperbolic, so Vol = 0; the non-linearity argument (permutation braids span H_3, s1 s2^-1 s1 s2^-1 closes to 4_1 with Vol 2.0299) is correct. Gap: the statement now also claims the result for the photon gamma = 1 + phi0 s0 + phi1 s1 + phi01 s0 s1^-1 (correct ruled form), whose vertex word s0 s1^-1 is not one of the two cases, yet the proof ends 'These are all the words in the support of gamma' and never treats s0 s1^-1 (its closure is the unknot, which the statement itself argues). The Vol = 0 convention for non-hyperbolic links is attributed to a conjecture block (conj:kashaev-volume-conjecture) rather than to the definition of hyperbolic volume. No empirical premise; no ruling conflict.
